- The change addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (0d737a8cfd83) that caused the workqueues to be freed too early. This modification is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the connection handling process in the DLM (Distributed Lock Manager) subsystem.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by freeing the workqueues in the `dlm_lowcomms_stop()` function before ensuring that all queued works were canceled. This premature freeing led to attempts to access already freed memory in the `free_conn()` function, resulting in potential memory corruption or crashes.
        
        Commit message:
        dlm: free workqueues after the connections

After backporting commit ee44b4bc054a ("dlm: use sctp 1-to-1 API")
series to a kernel with an older workqueue which didn't use RCU yet, it
was noticed that we are freeing the workqueues in dlm_lowcomms_stop()
too early as free_conn() will try to access that memory for canceling
the queued works if any.

This issue was introduced by commit 0d737a8cfd83 as before it such
attempt to cancel the queued works wasn't performed, so the issue was
not present.

This patch fixes it by simply inverting the free order.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 0d737a8cfd83 ("dlm: fix race while closing connections")
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Ricardo Leitner <marcelo.leitner@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David Teigland <teigland@redhat.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c b/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
index 963016c8f3d1..609998de533e 100644
--- a/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
+++ b/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
@@ -1656,16 +1656,12 @@ void dlm_lowcomms_stop(void)
 	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
 	dlm_allow_conn = 0;
 	foreach_conn(stop_conn);
+	clean_writequeues();
+	foreach_conn(free_conn);
 	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 
 	work_stop();
 
-	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
-	clean_writequeues();
-
-	foreach_conn(free_conn);
-
-	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 	kmem_cache_destroy(con_cache);
 }

dlm: free workqueues after the connections

After backporting commit ee44b4bc054a ("dlm: use sctp 1-to-1 API")
series to a kernel with an older workqueue which didn't use RCU yet, it
was noticed that we are freeing the workqueues in dlm_lowcomms_stop()
too early as free_conn() will try to access that memory for canceling
the queued works if any.

This issue was introduced by commit 0d737a8cfd83 as before it such
attempt to cancel the queued works wasn't performed, so the issue was
not present.

This patch fixes it by simply inverting the free order.

 	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 
 	work_stop();

-	clean_writequeues();
-
-	foreach_conn(free_conn);
-
-	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 	kmem_cache_destroy(con_cache);
 }

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
clean_writequeues();
foreach_conn(free_conn);
```
Reason:
The fix involves reordering the operations in `dlm_lowcomms_stop()` to ensure that `clean_writequeues()` and `foreach_conn(free_conn)` are called before freeing the workqueues. This guarantees that all queued works are canceled before the memory is freed, preventing access to already freed memory and thus avoiding the potential crashes or memory corruption.
